description:
Strong evidence that the number of concurrent streams a user requests never
reaches the throughput test, which silently runs at the hard-coded default
(2). Two independent breaks in the chain:

1. `run-official --streams N` VALIDATES that --streams is provided
   (benchbox/cli/commands/run_official.py:36-38), prints it (line 46, 52-53
   "Note: Stream configuration ({streams} streams) applies when supported"),
   then invokes `run` WITHOUT passing `streams`
   (run_official.py:56-67). The value is discarded.

2. Through the main pipeline, the run config carries `concurrent_streams`
   (from BenchmarkConfig.concurrency): benchbox/cli/execution_pipeline.py:106,
   benchbox/cli/orchestrator.py:494, benchbox/core/runner/runner.py:726,
   benchbox/core/schemas.py:98 (`RunConfig.concurrent_streams`). But the
   throughput drivers read a DIFFERENT key:
   - benchbox/platforms/base/execution.py:368
     `num_streams = run_config.get("num_streams", run_config.get("streams", 2))`
   - benchbox/platforms/base/execution.py:233 (TPC-DS) `run_config.get("num_streams", 2)`.
   Neither `num_streams` nor `streams` is ever populated from
   `concurrent_streams`, so both default to 2 regardless of user input.

Net effect: `benchbox run ... --phases throughput` and `run-official
--streams 8` both execute 2 streams. The headline throughput metric is
computed for the wrong concurrency level, and QphH/QphDS composed from it is
wrong. This is a functional defect, not just a UX gap.

NOTE (w0): confirm the break end-to-end with a live run before fixing, since
a legacy alias could exist somewhere not yet found. If a path is found that
DOES honor the count, narrow the fix accordingly.

anti_patterns.instead: map it at the driver boundary instead.
anti_patterns.why: it is used by cost models and result metrics

deferrals.reason:
run.py is not in this TODO's scope_limit.only_modify
(benchbox/platforms/base/execution.py,
benchbox/cli/commands/run_official.py, tests/integration/ only).
Adding a real CLI option there is a small, low-risk one-line-per-call
change (a new click.option + concurrency=... in the three
BenchmarkConfig(...) constructions in _run_dry_run/_run_direct/the
interactive flow) but is out of scope for this fix and needs its own
reviewed change.
deferrals.summary:
Add a --streams/--concurrency CLI option to `benchbox run` itself
(benchbox/cli/commands/run.py) so BenchmarkConfig.concurrency is
reachable from the canonical (non-deprecated) `run` command, not just
the deprecated `run-official` shim. Confirmed there is currently NO way
to set concurrency>1 through `run`'s direct-execution path
(benchbox/cli/commands/run.py `_run_direct`) at all -- every
`BenchmarkConfig(...)` construction in that file omits `concurrency=`,
so it always takes the schema default of 1. docs/usage/faq.md already
documents `benchbox run --platform duckdb --benchmark tpch --scale 1
--phases throughput --streams 4` as valid usage (see the sibling
concurrency-docs-alignment TODO's "do not document it as working until
it does" caveat) -- that example remains non-functional until this
follow-up lands, since run.py was out of this TODO's scope_limit.

preserves.behavior: Existing default of 2 streams when the user requests nothing.
back-compat callers that already pass num_streams= directly (official_benchmark.py path).

verifications.command: uv run -- python -m pytest tests/integration -k throughput_stream_count -v
verifications.description: Requesting N streams runs N streams against DuckDB
verifications.expected: test asserts streams_executed == requested N for N in {1,4}

work_units.notes:
Confirmed against a real (file-based) DuckDB TPC-H run (SF=0.01):
run_config carried concurrent_streams=4 (exactly what RunConfig
populates from BenchmarkConfig.concurrency), but
_execute_tpch_throughput_test only reads num_streams/streams, so
streams_executed=2 (the driver's own hardcoded default) regardless of
the request. Command + output captured to
/tmp/throughput-wiring-w0.log. This is now the regression oracle
exercised by tests/integration/test_throughput_stream_count.py.
work_units.summary: Prove the defect end-to-end: run throughput with --streams/concurrency=4 and assert only 2 streams execute today

work_units.notes:
Added a shared _resolve_requested_stream_count(run_config) helper in
benchbox/platforms/base/execution.py, used by both
_execute_tpch_throughput_test and _execute_tpcds_throughput_test.
Precedence: num_streams/streams (back-compat, existing callers/tests
that hand-build run_config) -> concurrent_streams (the canonical
RunConfig/BenchmarkConfig field) -> 2 (only when none of the three
keys are present at all, preserving must_preserve's back-compat
default for bare/legacy run_config dicts).
work_units.summary: Thread concurrent_streams -> num_streams through the adapter throughput drivers

work_units.notes:
Discovered run() (benchbox/cli/commands/run.py) has NO
--streams/--concurrency CLI option at all (out of this TODO's
scope_limit), so `streams` cannot be forwarded to ctx.invoke(run, ...)
as a keyword arg -- there's no matching parameter to receive it. Fixed
within run_official.py alone: added _forward_requested_streams(), a
context manager that transiently patches
BenchmarkOrchestrator.execute_benchmark (the one seam run()'s direct
execution path always passes through) to set
BenchmarkConfig.concurrency = streams immediately before execution --
the same canonical field the w1 driver fix reads, per
anti_patterns (no parallel field, no schema rename). Verified live via
`benchbox run-official tpch --platform duckdb --scale 1 --phases
throughput --streams 4 --seed 42`: BenchmarkOrchestrator.execute_benchmark
now observes config.concurrency == 4 (confirmed with a spy on the real
CLI path). Also replaced the misleading "applies when supported" note
with an accurate one. See the `deferred` section below for the
run.py-level gap this uncovered.
work_units.summary: Pass --streams from run-official into run (or route through the same concurrency field)

work_units.notes:
tests/integration/test_throughput_stream_count.py: real DuckDB TPC-H
(parametrized N in {1,4}) and TPC-DS (N=2) driver-level tests asserting
streams_executed == requested; a back-compat test confirming the
default of 2 is preserved when no stream-count key is present at all;
a back-compat test confirming num_streams= still wins over
concurrent_streams for legacy callers; and two focused tests of the
run_official.py _forward_requested_streams bridge (sets concurrency,
and is a no-op when --streams is absent). All 7 tests pass under the
canonical verification command.
work_units.summary: End-to-end regression test: requesting N streams executes N streams
